newsitem.title: JAPAN: Uruguay foreign minister to visit Japan.
newsitem.headline: Uruguay foreign minister to visit Japan.

text.p: Uruguay Foreign Minister Alvaro Ramos will visit Japan this week to explain his government's position on the Peru hostage crisis, Japanese Foreign Ministry officials said on Wednesday.
Ramos will meet Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda during his three-day visit starting on Friday, officials said.

The visit follows allegations that the Uruguay government struck a secret deal with leftist rebels holding scores of hostages in Lima to win the release of its ambassador to Peru, Tobare Bocalandro Yapeyu.
The Uruguay government has denied the allegations.

Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto last month expressed displeasure about Uruguay's release of two prisoners linked to the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels, saying the action did not help negotiations.
MRTA rebels still hold 81 hostages inside the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima.
After the release of the Uruguayan ambassador, Tokyo ordered its outgoing ambassador to Uruguay, Katsuhiko Tsunoda, to return home earlier than scheduled.
Japan's Foreign Ministry has denied the action was related to the Uruguayan envoy's release.
